messages.content: Please check this: Our science teacher gave us a informations sheet about volcanoes.

Our science teacher gave us an information sheet about volcanoes.
Why: Use "an" before a vowel sound. "Information" is uncountable, so it never takes -s.
Can you correct this? My aunt have two daughters and both of them is studying in Chennai.

My aunt has two daughters and both of them are studying in Chennai.
Why: "Aunt" is singular, so the verb is "has". "Both of them" is plural, so it needs "are".
What you would like to eat for dinner tonight? Is the word order right?

What would you like to eat for dinner tonight?
Why: In a question, the helper verb "would" comes before the subject "you".
We reached at the airport two hours before the flight. Is 'at' needed here?

No, remove it: We reached the airport two hours before the flight.
Why: "Reach" takes its object directly, so it needs no preposition. With "arrive" you would say "arrived at the airport".
The new manager came in and said us to sit down quietly. What's wrong here?

The new manager came in and told us to sit down quietly.
Why: "Tell" takes the person directly ("told us"). "Say" does not; you say something to someone.
The shopkeeper gave me a discount, so I paid less money than I had planned. Is this right?

This is already correct.
Why: "Money" is uncountable, so "less" is the right word. "Fewer" is used only with countable plural nouns. "Had planned" also correctly shows the earlier plan.
On Raksha Bandhan my sister ties a rakhi on my wrist and give me sweets. Please check.

On Raksha Bandhan my sister ties a rakhi on my wrist and gives me sweets.
Why: "My sister" is singular, so both verbs take -s: "ties" and "gives".
Our team losed the final but we played good. Correct this, please.

Our team lost the final but we played well.
Why: "Lose" is irregular, and its past tense is "lost". "Well" is the adverb that describes "played"; "good" is an adjective.
The monsoon reach Kerala on early June every year. Fix my sentence.

The monsoon reaches Kerala in early June every year.
Why: "Monsoon" is singular, so the present-tense verb takes -s. Use "in" with a month or part of a month; "on" is for a specific date.
Three of my favourite book's are on this shelf. What is wrong?

Three of my favourite books are on this shelf.
Why: A plural noun just adds -s. An apostrophe shows possession or a short form, never a plural.
I felt very embarrassing when everyone laughed at my answer. Is this right?

I felt very embarrassed when everyone laughed at my answer.
Why: An "-ed" adjective says how a person feels. An "-ing" adjective says what causes the feeling.
Anil and Sunita is my best friend. Please check my sentence.

Anil and Sunita are my best friends.
Why: Two people joined by "and" are plural, so the verb is "are" and the noun is "friends".
My phone is not working properly, I will buy new one tomorrow. Can you fix it?

My phone is not working properly, so I will buy a new one tomorrow.
Why: A comma alone cannot join two full sentences, so add "so". "New one" is singular and countable, so it needs "a".
Yesterday was a so cold day that we stayed inside. Correct me.

Yesterday was such a cold day that we stayed inside.
Why: Before "a + adjective + noun" use "such". "So" goes directly before an adjective, as in "so cold".
Please keep the books on the shelf and cleaning the table. Is this right?

Please keep the books on the shelf and clean the table.
Why: Two actions joined by "and" should have the same form. Both are commands here, so use "clean".
This is the more beautiful song I have ever heard. Check my grammar.

This is the most beautiful song I have ever heard.
Why: Comparing one song with all the others needs a superlative, "most beautiful". "More" compares only two things.
A cow give milk, and a hen lays egg. Please correct.

A cow gives milk, and a hen lays eggs.
Why: "Cow" is singular, so its verb takes -s. When we speak about eggs in general, we use the plural "eggs".
The traffic in our city are terrible in the morning. Is the verb right?

The traffic in our city is terrible in the morning.
Why: "Traffic" is uncountable and takes a singular verb. "Is" agrees with "traffic", not with "city".
I bought a new shirt, but it doesn't fit to me. What is the mistake?

I bought a new shirt, but it doesn't fit me.
Why: "Fit" takes its object directly, so "to" is not needed.
My grandfather goes for a walk every morning, and he feels fresh all day. Is this correct?

No change needed.
Why: "Grandfather" is singular, so "goes" and "feels" are right, and "go for a walk" is the normal phrase.
Our office is closed on Sundays, so we works from Monday to Saturday. Please check.

Our office is closed on Sundays, so we work from Monday to Saturday.
Why: "We" is plural, so the verb stays in its base form without -s.
We travelled by the bus to Mysore and returned by the train. What should it be?

We travelled by bus to Mysore and returned by train.
Why: After "by" with a means of transport, we use no article: "by bus", "by train".
Have you completed your homework yesterday? Fix it please.

Did you complete your homework yesterday?
Why: "Yesterday" names a finished time, so the question needs the simple past ("Did you complete"), not the present perfect.
My grandmother is telling us stories every night when we were young. Can you correct it?

My grandmother used to tell us stories every night when we were young.
Why: A repeated habit in the past is shown with "used to" (or the simple past "told"), not the present continuous.
I don't eat meat, neither my sister does. Is this right?

I don't eat meat, and neither does my sister.
Why: After "neither" the helper verb comes before the subject ("does my sister"), and "and" joins the two parts.
At Christmas, we decorate a small tree and make cards for our neighbours. Is this correct?

Yes, that's right.
Why: "Make" is the right verb for creating something, such as cards, and "decorate" and "make" both match the plural subject "we".
We didn't win the trophy, but we did our best. Is this right?

Nothing to fix here.
Why: "Do your best" is the fixed phrase, with do and not make. "Didn't win" correctly uses the base verb after "didn't".
The river flows under the bridge in a gentle speed. What's wrong?

The river flows under the bridge at a gentle speed.
Why: The preposition with speed is "at": we say "at a speed".
I borrowed this book to the library last week. Which word is wrong?

I borrowed this book from the library last week.
Why: You borrow something from a person or a place. The preposition "to" goes with "lend".
I am afraid of to speak in front of strangers. Please correct.

I am afraid of speaking in front of strangers.
Why: After a preposition such as "of", use the -ing form of the verb, not "to" plus the base form.
Deepa is the person who I can always rely. Fix it please.

Deepa is the person who I can always rely on.
Why: "Rely" is always followed by "on". The preposition stays after the verb even when "who" comes earlier.
My father pays the electricity bill in the first of every month. Correct this.

My father pays the electricity bill on the first of every month.
Why: Use "on" with dates and days, such as "on the first" or "on Monday".
The internet connection in our school are very slow today. Is the verb okay?

The internet connection in our school is very slow today.
Why: The verb agrees with the main noun "connection", which is singular, not with "school".
A cold wind was blowing and the sky is dark. Please fix the tense.

A cold wind was blowing and the sky was dark.
Why: Both parts describe the same moment in the past, so both verbs must be past: "was blowing" and "was".
He cleans the whole house himself, and nobody helps to him. Is this right?

He cleans the whole house himself, and nobody helps him.
Why: "Help" takes the person directly as its object, with no "to".
Listening to old songs make me remember my school days. Check this.

Listening to old songs makes me remember my school days.
Why: "Listening to old songs" acts as one singular subject, so the verb takes -s.
The cat jumped onto the shelf and knock down a glass. Fix the verb.

The cat jumped onto the shelf and knocked down a glass.
Why: "Jumped" is past, so the second verb joined by "and" must also be past.
Our city has many old temple and a big market. What is wrong?

Our city has many old temples and a big market.
Why: "Many" is followed by a plural noun, so "temple" becomes "temples".
My boss is very polite and never shouts to anyone. Is the preposition correct?

My boss is very polite and never shouts at anyone.
Why: When you raise your voice in anger at someone, use "shout at". "Shout to" means calling so that someone can hear you.
My school is nearer to my house than yours is. Is this right?

That sentence is correct.
Why: A comparative like "nearer" is followed by "than", and "to my house" is a correct preposition after "near".
Our exam starts from Monday and ends on Friday. Please check.

Our exam starts on Monday and ends on Friday.
Why: With a day of the week, use "on". "From" is for a range, as in "from Monday to Friday".
We visited our village for the Holi, and we play with colours. Please correct.

We visited our village for Holi, and we played with colours.
Why: Festival names take no article. The second verb must be past tense to match "visited".
We had a very tiring journey, so we slept early. Is this right?

Not quite: We had a very tiring journey, so we went to bed early.
Why: In standard English we "go to bed" early; "sleep early" is not used. "Tiring" is right because the journey causes the tiredness.
Their was a long queue at the ticket counter. Spelling please.

There was a long queue at the ticket counter.
Why: "There" is used to say that something exists. "Their" means belonging to them.
This wallet is made of leathers. Is that right?

This wallet is made of leather.
Why: A material such as leather is uncountable, so it has no plural form.
The principle of our school gave the prizes on Annual Day. Which word is wrong?

The principal of our school gave the prizes on Annual Day.
Why: "Principal" is the head of a school. "Principle" is a rule or a basic belief.
We walked threw the forest and saw many birds. Check the spelling.

We walked through the forest and saw many birds.
Why: "Through" means going in at one side and out at the other. "Threw" is the past tense of "throw".
I am very happy that you passed, and so is my mother. Is the last part right?

Yes, the last part is right.
Why: After "so" the helper verb comes before the subject, so "so is my mother" is right, and "is" agrees with the singular "mother".
Please inform to the office before you leave early. Fix this.

Please inform the office before you leave early.
Why: "Inform" is followed directly by the person or place, with no "to".
The childrens' playground is behind the library. Is the apostrophe right?

The children's playground is behind the library.
Why: "Children" is already plural, so the possessive is made with apostrophe + s: "children's".
Yesterday I go to the market and met my old teacher. Please correct.

Yesterday I went to the market and met my old teacher.
Why: "Yesterday" and "met" show the past, so "go" must also be in the past tense: "went".
I was cooking dinner when the phone was ringing. What should the last verb be?

I was cooking dinner when the phone rang.
Why: A short action that interrupts a longer one uses the simple past ("rang"). The longer action uses the past continuous ("was cooking").
How long are you living in this city? Check my question.

How long have you been living in this city?
Why: An action that began in the past and still continues uses the present perfect continuous with "how long".
He has been working here from 2018. Is 'from' right?

He has been working here since 2018.
Why: "Since" gives the starting point of a period that lasts up to now. "From" is used with an end point, as in "from 2018 to 2022".
The news about the exam results were shocking. Is the verb right?

The news about the exam results was shocking.
Why: "News" is uncountable and singular, so the verb is "was", even though the word ends in -s.
One of my friends are getting married next month. Please check.

One of my friends is getting married next month.
Why: The subject is "one", which is singular. "Of my friends" only describes it, so the verb is "is".
The scissors is on the table in the kitchen. Fix the verb, please.

The scissors are on the table in the kitchen.
Why: "Scissors" is a plural noun because it has two blades, so it takes "are".
What is the names of your teachers? Can you correct this question?

What are the names of your teachers?
Why: "Names" is plural, so the verb must be "are", not "is".
We watched a film yesterday. Film was very funny. What is missing?

We watched a film yesterday. The film was very funny.
Why: The second time we mention the film, it is a specific one that both people know, so it takes "the".
She is best singer in our school. Correct me.

She is the best singer in our school.
Why: A superlative such as "best" is normally preceded by "the", because it points to one particular singer.
It was a honour to meet your grandfather. Is 'a' right?

It was an honour to meet your grandfather.
Why: "Honour" begins with a vowel sound because the "h" is silent, so the article is "an".
Delhi is capital of India. Is the grammar right?

Delhi is the capital of India.
Why: India has only one capital, so it is a specific, unique thing and needs "the".
She is interested in painting and good at drawing animals. Is this correct?

Both prepositions are right, so no change is needed.
Why: "Interested" is followed by "in" and "good" by "at", so both prepositions are right.
I am fond for dancing and singing. Please check.

I am fond of dancing and singing.
Why: The adjective "fond" is followed by "of", not "for".
I still depend of my parents for pocket money. What is wrong?

I still depend on my parents for pocket money.
Why: The verb "depend" takes the preposition "on".
Please pay attention at the teacher. Which word is wrong?

Please pay attention to the teacher.
Why: The phrase is "pay attention to", not "at".
The ball rolled off the table and fell in the floor. Fix the preposition.

The ball rolled off the table and fell on the floor.
Why: Use "on" for a surface such as a floor or a table. "In" is for something inside a space.
I always drink tea in the morning. Is 'always' in the right place?

Your word order is fine.
Why: A frequency word like "always" goes after the subject and before the main verb, so the word order is right.
How you reached here so early? Please fix my question.

How did you reach here so early?
Why: A question with "how" needs the helper "did" before the subject, and then the main verb goes back to the base form "reach".
I every day walk to school. Is the order okay?

I walk to school every day.
Why: The verb comes right after the subject, and a time phrase such as "every day" usually goes at the end.
She speaks very well English. Please fix the word order.

She speaks English very well.
Why: The object "English" must stay next to the verb. The adverb phrase "very well" comes after it.
We bought some new furnitures for the living room. Please correct.

We bought some new furniture for the living room.
Why: "Furniture" is uncountable, so it has no plural form. You can say "pieces of furniture" to count it.
We saw two deers near the lake. What is wrong?

We saw two deer near the lake.
Why: "Deer" has the same form in the singular and the plural.
Several woman in our colony have started a small library. Is it correct?

Several women in our colony have started a small library.
Why: "Several" is followed by a plural noun, and the plural of "woman" is the irregular form "women".
Our new teacher is less stricter than the old one. Please correct.

Our new teacher is less strict than the old one.
Why: After "less" use the plain adjective. "Stricter" already contains the idea of "more", so the two do not go together.
Of the two sisters, Gita is the oldest. Is that right?

Of the two sisters, Gita is the older.
Why: When you compare only two people, use the comparative "older". The superlative "oldest" is for three or more.
He is as tall as his father now. Is this sentence right?

Correct as it stands.
Why: "As ... as" is the right pattern to say two things are equal, so "as tall as" is correct.
She made the poster by her own. What should it be?

She made the poster on her own.
Why: Use "on her own" or "by herself" to mean without help. "By her own" mixes the two patterns.
He looked at him in the mirror and smiled. Is 'him' right here?

If "him" means the same person as "he", change it to "himself": He looked at himself in the mirror and smiled.
Why: When the subject and the object are the same person, English uses a reflexive pronoun.
Is this pen your or mine? Fix my question.

Is this pen yours or mine?
Why: When no noun follows, use the possessive pronoun "yours". "Your" needs a noun after it.
Everyone should bring their own water bottle on the trip. Is 'their' okay here?

Yes, 'their' is fine here.
Why: "Their" is the normal modern pronoun for "everyone" when the gender is not known.
Can you advice me on which colour to paint the wall? Check my spelling.

Can you advise me on which colour to paint the wall?
Why: "Advise" with an s is the verb. "Advice" with a c is the noun, as in "some advice".
I need to buy some stationary for school tomorrow. Is the word right?

I need to buy some stationery for school tomorrow.
Why: "Stationery" means pens, paper and similar things. "Stationary" means not moving.
The heavy rain had a big affect on the crops. Please correct.

The heavy rain had a big effect on the crops.
Why: After "a big" we need a noun. "Effect" is the noun, and "affect" is the verb.
We walked passed the old fort on our way home. Check the spelling.

We walked past the old fort on our way home.
Why: "Past" is the preposition meaning "beyond". "Passed" is the past tense of the verb "pass".
Ravi is tall, his brother is short. What is wrong with the comma?

Ravi is tall, but his brother is short.
Why: A comma alone cannot join two full sentences. Add a linking word such as "but" to show the contrast.
The dogs bowl is empty, so please fill it. Is there a mistake?

The dog's bowl is empty, so please fill it.
Why: One dog owns the bowl, so the possessive needs an apostrophe before the s: "dog's".
Its going to be very hot today, so carry water. Please correct.

It's going to be very hot today, so carry water.
Why: "It's" is the short form of "it is". "Its" without an apostrophe shows possession.
I need to do a phone call before the meeting starts. Is 'do' right?

I need to make a phone call before the meeting starts.
Why: The fixed phrase is "make a phone call". We do not use "do" with call.
Let's do a plan for the weekend. What is wrong?

Let's make a plan for the weekend.
Why: We "make" plans, not "do" them. "Make a plan" is the fixed phrase.
Please make me a favour and lock the gate. Correct it please.

Please do me a favour and lock the gate.
Why: The fixed phrase is "do someone a favour", not "make".
My sister is doing a cake for my birthday. Fix the verb.

My sister is making a cake for my birthday.
Why: "Make" is the verb for preparing or creating something, such as a cake.
The teacher told good morning and we all stood up. Is 'told' right?

The teacher said good morning and we all stood up.
Why: Greetings go with "say". "Tell" needs a person right after it, as in "told us".
It is dark in here, please open the light. Fix this.

It is dark in here, so please switch on the light.
Why: Lights are switched on or turned on. "Open" is for doors, windows and books. A comma alone also cannot join two full sentences, so "so" is added.
Please stop to make noise, the baby is sleeping. Correct, please.

Please stop making noise because the baby is sleeping.
Why: "Stop" plus -ing means to quit an activity ("stop to" means stopping in order to do something). "Because" is needed, as a comma alone cannot join two sentences.
I remember to meet him in Pune last year. What is the right form?

I remember meeting him in Pune last year.
Why: "Remember" plus -ing is a memory of something that happened. "Remember to" is for something you must still do.
I am thinking to buy a bicycle next month. Please check.

I am thinking of buying a bicycle next month.
Why: "Think of" is followed by the -ing form of the verb, not by "to".
I want that you come with me to the station. Is this correct English?

I want you to come with me to the station.
Why: "Want" takes an object followed by "to" plus the base verb. It cannot be followed by "that".
My good name is Kiran and I am in class ten. Can you check my introduction?

My name is Kiran and I am in class ten.
Why: In standard English we say "my name". "Good name" is not used when you introduce yourself.
He is my cousin brother and lives in Madurai. Please fix it.

He is my cousin and lives in Madurai.
Why: "Cousin" already covers both a male and a female relative, so "brother" is not added.
I passed out from college in 2020 and joined a firm. Please check this line.

I graduated from college in 2020 and joined a firm.
Why: In standard English "pass out" means to faint. To say you finished a course, use "graduate from".
Kindly revert back to me by Friday. Is this correct?

Kindly reply to me by Friday.
Why: "Revert" means to return to an earlier state, so it is not used for answering. Use "reply" or "get back to me".
If I was you, I would say sorry to her. Is 'was' right?

If I were you, I would say sorry to her.
Why: An imaginary situation in the present uses "were" for every subject, even "I", in careful English.
Neither of my parents are at home right now. Please correct.

Neither of my parents is at home right now.
Why: In careful English "neither" means "not one of the two", so it takes a singular verb: "is".
A bunch of keys were found on the bus. What is wrong?

A bunch of keys was found on the bus.
Why: The verb agrees with the main noun "bunch", which is singular, not with "keys".
She scored a high marks in the science test. Check please.

She scored high marks in the science test.
Why: "Marks" is plural, so the article "a" cannot go before it. Without the article the sentence is correct.
He has few patience, so he gets angry quickly. Fix it.

He has little patience, so he gets angry quickly.
Why: "Patience" is uncountable, so use "little", not "few". "Few" goes with countable plural nouns.
Suresh is more intelligent than any boy in his class. Is this right?

Suresh is more intelligent than any other boy in his class.
Why: Suresh is himself a boy in the class. Without "other", the sentence compares him with himself.
The more you practise, the better you will play. Is this correct?

Yes, this is already right.
Why: The pattern "the + comparative, the + comparative" shows that two things change together, and "practise" is the correct spelling of the verb in British English.
She apologised me for being late. What is missing?

She apologised to me for being late.
Why: "Apologise" takes "to" before the person and "for" before the reason.
Please give a call me when you reach home. Fix the order.

Please give me a call when you reach home.
Why: When a verb has two objects, the person usually comes first: "give me a call".
I will meet you at the libary at four. Check my spelling.

I will meet you at the library at four.
Why: "Library" has two r's: li-bra-ry. Many people drop the first r.
Please recieve the parcel from the postman. Is the spelling right?

Please receive the parcel from the postman.
Why: The rule is "i before e, except after c", so after "c" the letters are "ei": receive.
We have a seperate room for guests. What is wrong with the spelling?

We have a separate room for guests.
Why: The middle of the word is "-para-", not "-pera-". It helps to remember "a rat" in "separate".
The tourists rode camels across the dessert. Which word is wrong?

The tourists rode camels across the desert.
Why: "Desert", spelled with one s, is dry, sandy land. "Dessert", with a double s, is a sweet dish eaten after a meal.
She wore a lovely dress to the wedding, but it was to big. Please correct.

She wore a lovely dress to the wedding, but it was too big.
Why: "Too" means more than is needed. "To" is a preposition or part of an infinitive.
The farmer feeds his cattles twice a day. Is the plural right?

The farmer feeds his cattle twice a day.
Why: "Cattle" is already a plural noun, so it never takes -s.
Many peoples came to the fair on Sunday. What should it be?

Many people came to the fair on Sunday.
Why: "People" is already the plural of "person". "Peoples" is used only for different nations or groups.
I wanted to go, however it was raining. Please correct the punctuation.

I wanted to go; however, it was raining.
Why: "However" is not a conjunction, so a comma alone cannot join the two sentences. Use a semicolon before it and a comma after it, or use "but" instead.
I lost the bus, so I walked to the office. Is 'lost' right?

I missed the bus, so I walked to the office.
Why: You "miss" a bus or train that you fail to catch. "Lose" is for things you can no longer find or keep.
I will give the exam tomorrow. Please check my sentence.

I will take the exam tomorrow.
Why: A student "takes" an exam. "Give an exam" is what the teacher does when they set it.
He spoke a lie about the broken vase. Fix it.

He told a lie about the broken vase.
Why: The fixed phrase is "tell a lie". "Speak" is used for languages and speeches.
I go to the market for buying vegetables every Sunday. Is it correct?

I go to the market to buy vegetables every Sunday.
Why: To give a purpose, use "to" plus the base verb, not "for" plus -ing.
He decided going to Mumbai after college. Please correct.

He decided to go to Mumbai after college.
Why: The verb "decide" is followed by "to" plus the base verb.
He is capable to do this job alone. What is wrong?

He is capable of doing this job alone.
Why: The adjective "capable" is followed by "of" and the -ing form.
A new girl joined our class. She's name is Pooja. Please check.

A new girl joined our class. Her name is Pooja.
Why: "She's" means "she is". To show that the name belongs to her, use the possessive "her".
I met the boy who bicycle was stolen. Which word is wrong?

I met the boy whose bicycle was stolen.
Why: "Whose" shows that something belongs to a person. "Who" is the subject of a verb.
She is the girl which won the prize. Is 'which' right?

She is the girl who won the prize.
Why: Use "who" for people. "Which" is for things and animals.
I have been waiting here for an hour, and the bus has not come yet. Is this correct?

It is right as it is.
Why: "Have been waiting" shows an action that started earlier and still goes on, and "for an hour" gives its length. "Has not come yet" correctly uses the present perfect.
She plays violin beautifully. What is missing?

She plays the violin beautifully.
Why: In British and Indian English we usually say "play the" before a musical instrument.
What a nice weather we are having today! Please correct.

What nice weather we are having today!
Why: "Weather" is uncountable, so it cannot take "a".
She has a long black hair. Is it right?

She has long black hair.
Why: "Hair" as a whole is uncountable, so it takes no "a". "A hair" would mean a single strand.
I want to be pilot when I grow up. Please correct.

I want to be a pilot when I grow up.
Why: A singular job title needs an article, so use "a pilot".
The bus had left before I reach the stop. Fix the tense.

The bus had left before I reached the stop.
Why: The earlier event uses the past perfect ("had left") and the later event uses the simple past ("reached").
The tea is not enough hot. Please fix the order.

The tea is not hot enough.
Why: "Enough" comes after an adjective, not before it.
She sings so well that everyone stops to listen. Is this right?

That is correct; nothing to change.
Why: "So + adverb + that" is the correct pattern for a result, and "stops to listen" means people stop in order to listen.
I am late because of the lift was broken. Is 'because of' right?

I am late because the lift was broken.
Why: "Because of" is followed by a noun phrase. Before a full clause with a subject and verb, use "because".
I called him yesterday night, but he did not answer. Please check.

I called him last night, but he did not answer.
Why: "Last night" is the fixed phrase. "Yesterday night" is not used in standard English.
You are coming to the party tomorrow, isn't it? Is the end right?

You are coming to the party tomorrow, aren't you?
Why: A question tag repeats the helper verb of the sentence with a pronoun, so "are" gives "aren't you". "Isn't it" cannot be used for every sentence.
It is late. Let's go to home now. What is wrong?

It is late. Let's go home now.
Why: "Home" is an adverb here, so it needs no "to".
I walk for an hour everyday after dinner. Is 'everyday' right?

I walk for an hour every day after dinner.
Why: As an adverb of time, "every day" is two words. "Everyday" is one word only when it is an adjective meaning ordinary.
I like mangoes alot. Please check the spelling.

I like mangoes a lot.
Why: "A lot" is always two words. "Alot" is not a word in standard English, so it should be written with a space.
I will definately visit you in Pune. Spelling, please.

I will definitely visit you in Pune.
Why: The word is spelled "definitely", with "-ite-" in the middle, not "-ate-".
The final match is on Wensday. Check my spelling.

The final match is on Wednesday.
Why: "Wednesday" has a silent d, which is easy to forget. Say it as Wenz-day but spell it Wed-nes-day.
Their going to arrive by noon. Is it correct?

They're going to arrive by noon.
Why: "They're" is the short form of "they are". "Their" shows that something belongs to them.
I saved enough pocket money to buy a new bat. Is this right?

This sentence is fine as written.
Why: "Enough" goes before a noun, and "to buy" gives the purpose.
The parrot repeated everything we said, and it made us laugh. Is this right?

No mistake here; it is correct.
Why: After "made" plus an object, we use the base verb without "to", so "made us laugh" is right.
My uncle learned me how to ride a bicycle. Please correct.

My uncle taught me how to ride a bicycle.
Why: "Teach" means to give knowledge to someone else. "Learn" means to get knowledge yourself.
My phone's battery got finished so I could not call you. Please fix.

My phone's battery ran out, so I could not call you.
Why: The usual phrase is "run out", as in "the battery ran out". A comma before "so" also helps to separate the two parts.
She is not feeling well, so she is taking rest at home. Is the last part right?

She is not feeling well, so she is resting at home.
Why: "Rest" works as a verb. The noun phrase needs an article, as in "taking a rest", so "taking rest" is not standard.
At dusk we lit candles along the steps, and the house looked lovely. Is this right?

Yes, you wrote it correctly.
Why: "Lit" is the correct past tense of "light", and "looked" is followed by the adjective "lovely".
I am not understanding this chapter. Can you explain it?

I do not understand this chapter. Can you explain it?
Why: "Understand" is a stative verb, which describes a state of mind, so it is not normally used in the continuous form.
I am waiting for this bus for half an hour. What is wrong?

I have been waiting for this bus for half an hour.
Why: An action that began in the past and is still going on uses the present perfect continuous, especially with "for" and a length of time.
It is the first time I eat this sweet. Please check my tense.

It is the first time I have eaten this sweet.
Why: After "It is the first time" we use the present perfect, "have eaten".
The number of students in our club are increasing. Is the verb right?

The number of students in our club is increasing.
Why: "The number of" is singular, so it takes "is". "A number of" would take a plural verb.
Where is my sandals? I left them here. Please correct my question.

Where are my sandals? I left them here.
Why: "Sandals" is plural, so the verb must be "are".
Half of the cake were eaten before the guests arrived. Fix it.

Half of the cake was eaten before the guests arrived.
Why: With "half of", the verb agrees with the noun after it. "Cake" is singular, so it is "was".
The Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world. What should I change?

Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
Why: The name of a single mountain takes no article, so remove the first "the". The superlative "the highest" keeps its "the".
We visited Taj Mahal on our school trip. Is an article missing?

We visited the Taj Mahal on our school trip.
Why: Names of famous buildings and monuments usually take "the".
Moon is shining brightly tonight. Please correct.

The moon is shining brightly tonight.
Why: There is only one moon that we all know, so it takes "the".
We congratulated Dev on his success in the quiz. Is this correct?

Yes, "on" is the right word.
Why: We "congratulate someone on" something, so "on" is the right preposition.
She is very proud for her daughter. Which word is wrong?

She is very proud of her daughter.
Why: The adjective "proud" is followed by "of".
Don't laugh on other people's mistakes. Fix the preposition.

Don't laugh at other people's mistakes.
Why: The verb "laugh" takes "at" when you laugh about someone or something.
He was absent in class yesterday. Is 'in' right?

He was absent from class yesterday.
Why: The adjective "absent" is followed by "from".
The mango was full with juice. Please check.

The mango was full of juice.
Why: The adjective "full" is followed by "of".
I have no interest on sports. What is wrong?

I have no interest in sports.
Why: The noun "interest" takes the preposition "in".
The bus arrived to the village at night. Correct the preposition.

The bus arrived at the village at night.
Why: "Arrive" is followed by "at" for a small place or "in" for a city or country. It is never followed by "to".
Who you are waiting for? Correct my question.

Who are you waiting for?
Why: In a question the helper verb "are" comes before the subject "you".
What means this word? Please fix my question.

What does this word mean?
Why: A question needs the helper "does" before the subject. Then the main verb returns to the base form, "mean".
Could you tell me where the post office is? Is this correct?

This is already well formed.
Why: In an indirect question the subject comes before the verb, as in a statement, so "where the post office is" is the right order.
I have two sister-in-laws in Pune. Is the plural right?

I have two sisters-in-law in Pune.
Why: In compound nouns like this one, the main noun takes the plural: "sisters-in-law".
The tomatos are cheap at the market today. Check the spelling.

The tomatoes are cheap at the market today.
Why: Many nouns that end in -o after a consonant take -es in the plural, as in tomato and tomatoes.
Five thousands people came to the fair. Please correct.

Five thousand people came to the fair.
Why: After a number, "thousand" stays singular. It takes -s only in phrases like "thousands of people".
I have many works to finish before the weekend. What is wrong?

I have a lot of work to finish before the weekend.
Why: "Work" meaning tasks is uncountable, so it has no plural and cannot follow "many".
Of all my cousins, Rhea is the funniest. Is this right?

Yes, "the funniest" is correct.
Why: The superlative "funniest" with "the" is right when one person is compared with a whole group.
The weather today is better than yesterday. Is the comparison right?

The weather today is better than yesterday's.
Why: A comparison should set like things side by side: today's weather with yesterday's weather, not with a day.
My friend and myself went to the fair. Fix it, please.

My friend and I went to the fair.
Why: "Myself" is a reflexive pronoun and needs an earlier "I" in the sentence. As a subject, use "I".
Our teacher is very strict about grammer. Check the spelling.

Our teacher is very strict about grammar.
Why: "Grammar" ends in -ar, not -er.
He is writting a letter to his pen friend. Spelling, please.

He is writing a letter to his pen friend.
Why: When "write" takes -ing, the final e is dropped and the t is not doubled: writing.
The power cut occured at midnight. Is the spelling right?

The power cut occurred at midnight.
Why: "Occur" ends in a stressed vowel plus a consonant, so the r is doubled before -ed.
Yesterday I choose the green kurta for the party. Please correct.

Yesterday I chose the green kurta for the party.
Why: "Yesterday" shows the past, and the past tense of "choose" is "chose".
It was hard to breath in all that smoke. Which word is wrong?

It was hard to breathe in all that smoke.
Why: "Breathe" with an e is the verb. "Breath" without the e is the noun.
I don't know wear I kept my specs. Spelling please.

I don't know where I kept my specs.
Why: "Where" asks about a place. "Wear" means to have clothes on your body.
Could I have a peace of cake? Is the word right?

Could I have a piece of cake?
Why: "Piece" means a part of something. "Peace" means calm and quiet.
Ravis uncle came to see us yesterday. What is missing?

Ravi's uncle came to see us yesterday.
Why: An apostrophe and s show that the uncle belongs to Ravi.
The two boy's bags are still in the classroom. Check the apostrophe.

The two boys' bags are still in the classroom.
Why: There are two boys, so the plural is "boys", and the apostrophe comes after the s to show possession.
The principal did a short speech on Annual Day. Is 'did' right?

The principal gave a short speech on Annual Day.
Why: A speech is "given" or "made", not "done". You can also say "made a short speech".
Please do silence in the library. Can you correct this?

Please keep silent in the library.
Why: The usual phrase is "keep silent" or "keep quiet". We do not say "do silence".
He did a bad decision when he left the project. Please fix the verb.

He made a bad decision when he left the project.
Why: We "make" a decision. "Make" is the verb used with decisions, plans and choices.
You should do more effort in maths. What is wrong?

You should make more effort in maths.
Why: The fixed phrase is "make an effort", not "do an effort".
My parents don't allow me to stay out late. Is this right?

Your sentence is correct.
Why: "Allow" is followed by an object and "to" plus the base verb, so "allow me to stay" is correct.
I would rather to stay home today. Please correct.

I would rather stay home today.
Why: After "would rather" use the base verb without "to".
I am interested to join the chess club. Is it correct?

I am interested in joining the chess club.
Why: The adjective "interested" is followed by "in" and the -ing form.
The dog started to barking when the stranger came. Fix this.

The dog started barking when the stranger came.
Why: "Started" can be followed by -ing ("started barking") or by "to" plus the base verb ("started to bark"), but not "to" plus -ing.
Last Eid my cousins comes from Hyderabad and stayed with us. Please check.

Last Eid my cousins came from Hyderabad and stayed with us.
Why: "Last Eid" is in the past, so "comes" must be past tense, "came", to match "stayed".
Our captain, he is a very brave player. What is wrong?

Our captain is a very brave player.
Why: The subject "our captain" is already stated, so we do not repeat it with "he".
There have been a lot of rain this week. Is the verb right?

There has been a lot of rain this week.
Why: "Rain" is uncountable and singular, so the verb is "has been".
I am saving money to buy a gift to my mother. Which word is wrong?

I am saving money to buy a gift for my mother.
Why: A gift meant for someone is "a gift for" that person. We use "give to" for the act of handing it over.
I miss to talk to her every day. Please correct.

I miss talking to her every day.
Why: The verb "miss" is followed by the -ing form, not by "to".
My brother is expert in video editing. Is an article missing?

My brother is an expert in video editing.
Why: "Expert" is a singular noun here, so it needs the article "an".
Please check this: We have visited Agra last summer and saw the Taj Mahal at sunrise.

We visited Agra last summer and saw the Taj Mahal at sunrise.
Why: A finished time such as "last summer" needs the simple past, not the present perfect.
Is the second part okay? When I will reach home, I will call you.

When I reach home, I will call you.
Why: After "when" in a clause about the future, use the present simple, not "will".
What's the proper way to say this? My manager is working here since last March.

My manager has been working here since last March.
Why: "Since" a starting point needs the present perfect continuous, not the present continuous.
Our team didn't played well, so we lose the semi-final. Please proofread.

Our team didn't play well, so we lost the semi-final.
Why: After "didn't" use the base verb "play". The story is in the past, so "lose" becomes "lost".
Is the verb okay in this? A plate of samosas are on the kitchen table.

A plate of samosas is on the kitchen table.
Why: The subject is "plate", which is singular, so the verb is "is". The word "samosas" only describes what is on it.
Which verb should I use here: Neither Mia nor her sisters was at the party?

Neither Mia nor her sisters were at the party.
Why: With "neither ... nor" the verb agrees with the nearer subject. "Sisters" is plural, so use "were".
My grandparents lives near the temple and walks there daily. Could you proofread it?

My grandparents live near the temple and walk there daily.
Why: "Grandparents" is plural, so both verbs drop the -s.
Every one of the trees in our street have been painted white. Spot the mistake.

Every one of the trees in our street has been painted white.
Why: "Every one" is singular, so the helper verb is "has", even though "trees" comes just before it.
Something seems missing before "engineer": She works as engineer in a software company.

She works as an engineer in a software company.
Why: A job title after "as" takes "a" or "an", and "an" is used before the vowel sound in "engineer".
Is "an one-day trip" right? We took an one-day trip to the beach.

We took a one-day trip to the beach.
Why: Use "a" before a word that begins with a consonant sound. "One" starts with a "w" sound.
Check this for me: I love reading the poetry in the evenings.

I love reading poetry in the evenings.
Why: Do not use "the" before an uncountable noun like "poetry" when you mean it in general.
On the Independence Day, our school hoists the flag and sings the anthem. What needs to change?

On Independence Day, our school hoists the flag and sings the anthem.
Why: Names of days such as Independence Day usually take no article.
Correct my preposition, please: I have been friends with Zara from five years.

I have been friends with Zara for five years.
Why: Use "for" with a length of time, and "since" with a starting point.
My brother is jealous from my new bicycle. Is there a mistake?

My brother is jealous of my new bicycle.
Why: The adjective "jealous" is followed by "of".
He is addicted to play online games, so he saves no money. What should be fixed?

He is addicted to playing online games, so he saves no money.
Why: In "addicted to", the word "to" is a preposition, so the verb after it takes -ing.
Should it be "in" or "on"? She hung the painting in the wall above the sofa.

She hung the painting on the wall above the sofa.
Why: Use "on" for something fixed to a surface such as a wall.
Why she is crying in the garden? Please fix my question.

Why is she crying in the garden?
Why: In a direct question the verb "is" comes before the subject "she".
Can you tell me what time does the library open? Is this fine?

Can you tell me what time the library opens?
Why: Inside an indirect question, use the normal statement order, so "does" is dropped and the verb takes -s.
How often you visit your grandparents? Fix the question for me.

How often do you visit your grandparents?
Why: Questions with "how often" need the helper verb "do" before the subject "you".
We packed too many luggage for a two-day trip. Is "many" right?

We packed too much luggage for a two-day trip.
Why: "Luggage" is uncountable, so it takes "much", not "many".
The teacher corrected all our homework and gave us a feedback. Anything wrong?

The teacher corrected all our homework and gave us feedback.
Why: "Feedback" is uncountable, so it takes no "a".
Three wolfs were seen near the village last night. Is the plural right?

Three wolves were seen near the village last night.
Why: Many nouns ending in -f change to -ves in the plural, so "wolf" becomes "wolves".
There are many tomatos and potatos in the basket. What's off about the spelling?

There are many tomatoes and potatoes in the basket.
Why: Nouns ending in a consonant plus -o usually add -es in the plural.
This is the most good game I have ever watched. Please correct it.

This is the best game I have ever watched.
Why: "Good" has the irregular superlative "best", so "most good" is not used.
Neither of the two rooms is as bigger as the hall. Correct this, please.

Neither of the two rooms is as big as the hall.
Why: In "as ... as" comparisons the adjective stays in its base form.
It was hotter and more hotter every day in May. What is the error?

It was hotter and hotter every day in May.
Why: A short adjective takes -er, so "more hotter" is a double comparison. Repeat "hotter" to show it is increasing.
Rahul and Priya cooked dinner by theirselves. Can you fix the last word?

Rahul and Priya cooked dinner by themselves.
Why: The reflexive pronoun for "they" is "themselves". "Theirselves" is not standard English.
The teacher gave Anil and I some extra books. Is that correct?

The teacher gave Anil and me some extra books.
Why: "Anil and me" are the objects of "gave", so the object pronoun "me" is needed.
This umbrella is her, not mine. Which word needs to change?

This umbrella is hers, not mine.
Why: When no noun follows, the possessive pronoun is "hers", not "her".
The children brought they're own lunch to the picnic. Spelling or grammar?

The children brought their own lunch to the picnic.
Why: "Their" shows ownership. "They're" is only short for "they are".
I cut me while chopping onions. Is that okay?

I cut myself while chopping onions.
Why: When the subject and the object are the same person, use the reflexive pronoun "myself".
I want to learn how to right a good essay. Which word is wrong?

I want to learn how to write a good essay.
Why: "Write" is the verb for putting words on paper. "Right" means correct.
We spent the whole day on a beautiful beech near Puri. Please check my spelling.

We spent the whole day on a beautiful beach near Puri.
Why: A "beach" is sand by the sea. A "beech" is a type of tree.
Please keep the recipt for the bill. How do I spell this word?

Please keep the receipt for the bill.
Why: "Receipt" has a silent "p" and the order "ei" after "c".
I will meat you at the station at six. Is that the right word?

I will meet you at the station at six.
Why: "Meet" means to come together with someone. "Meat" is food from animals.
Dear Meera I hope you are well and enjoying your holidays. Fix the punctuation.

Dear Meera, I hope you are well and enjoying your holidays.
Why: Put a comma after the name in a greeting.
Please sit down said the teacher. What is missing?

"Please sit down," said the teacher.
Why: Spoken words go inside quotation marks, with a comma before the closing mark.
I bought apples oranges bananas and grapes from the stall. Can you add what is missing?

I bought apples, oranges, bananas and grapes from the stall.
Why: Commas separate the items in a list.
Please say the truth about what happened to the window. Is "say" right?

Please tell the truth about what happened to the window.
Why: "Tell the truth" is the fixed phrase. "Say the truth" is not standard.
We had strong rain on the way home. Is that the right word?

We had heavy rain on the way home.
Why: "Heavy" is the word that usually goes with rain. "Strong" is used with wind.
My grandmother makes me company when I am alone at home. Please check.

My grandmother keeps me company when I am alone at home.
Why: The fixed phrase is "keep someone company".
My neighbour has a large experience in teaching. Can you improve this?

My neighbour has a lot of experience in teaching.
Why: "Experience" in this sense is uncountable, and "a lot of" is the usual partner for it, not "large".
The referee denied to give a penalty. Should the verb change?

The referee refused to give a penalty.
Why: "Deny" means to say something is not true, so it changed the meaning. "Refuse" is followed by "to" and the base verb.
Would you like that I help you carry the bags? Is this natural?

Would you like me to help you carry the bags?
Why: "Would like" is followed by an object and "to", not by a "that" clause.
Mehul is busy to prepare for his exams this week. Please correct the verb.

Mehul is busy preparing for his exams this week.
Why: "Busy" is followed by an -ing form.
Is the word order right here? Do you know what is in this curry?

Yes, that's right.
Why: In an indirect question after "Do you know", normal statement order is used. "What" is the subject, so no extra helper verb is needed.
Can you check the prepositions? The train to Pune leaves from platform four at half past six.

No change needed.
Why: "From platform four" gives the place and "at half past six" gives the clock time, so both prepositions are correct.
Is "my cousin and I" okay as the subject? My cousin and I walked to the lake after breakfast.

This is already correct.
Why: "I" is the subject pronoun, and putting the other person first is the usual polite order.
Is "allergic to" the right pair? She is allergic to dust, so she keeps her windows closed.

Yes, it is.
Why: The standard preposition after "allergic" is "to", and "keeps her windows closed" is a normal pattern.
Does this conditional sentence look right? If it rains tomorrow, we will move the picnic to Sunday.

Looks good as it is.
Why: The "if" clause uses the present simple and the main clause uses "will", which is the normal pattern for a real future possibility. Nothing needs to change.
What should the verb be in the second half? If she had more time, she will learn the violin.

If she had more time, she would learn the violin.
Why: An unreal present condition uses the past in the "if" clause and "would" in the main clause.
Whenever it rained, the road is flooded for hours. Please make the tenses match.

Whenever it rained, the road was flooded for hours.
Why: The sentence is about the past, so the second verb must be past too.
I used to played cricket every evening before the exams. Is this right?

I used to play cricket every evening before the exams.
Why: After "used to" the verb stays in the base form.
Have you ate lunch yet? Please correct my question.

Have you eaten lunch yet?
Why: The present perfect needs the past participle "eaten", not the past form "ate".
The pair of shoes under the bed are mine. Is the verb right?

The pair of shoes under the bed is mine.
Why: The subject is "pair", which is singular, so the verb is "is".
Does your brothers play chess at school? Fix my question, please.

Do your brothers play chess at school?
Why: "Brothers" is plural, so the helper verb is "do", not "does".
Everybody were clapping when the singer walked on stage. Anything to change?

Everybody was clapping when the singer walked on stage.
Why: "Everybody" is singular, so it takes "was".
The police is searching the market for the missing child. Is the verb correct?

The police are searching the market for the missing child.
Why: "Police" is always plural, so the verb is "are".
We saw lion and tiger at the zoo yesterday. Something is missing.

We saw a lion and a tiger at the zoo yesterday.
Why: Singular countable nouns need an article.
I am learning the Spanish on weekends. Please fix it.

I am learning Spanish on weekends.
Why: The names of languages take no article, so "the" is dropped before "Spanish".
There was power cut for two hours last night. What is missing?

There was a power cut for two hours last night.
Why: "Power cut" is a singular countable noun, so it needs "a".
Please pass me a salt. Is that right?

Please pass me the salt.
Why: "Salt" is uncountable, so it cannot take "a". "The" points to the salt on the table.
The Ganga is longest river in India. Please correct it.

The Ganga is the longest river in India.
Why: A superlative such as "longest" is used with "the".
We play cricket in Sundays at the park. Which word is wrong?

We play cricket on Sundays at the park.
Why: Use "on" with days of the week.
My house is next the post office. What is missing?

My house is next to the post office.
Why: The correct phrase is "next to".
I am tired from this noise. Is the preposition right?

I am tired of this noise.
Why: "Tired of" means annoyed by something. "Tired from" is used after effort, such as a long walk.
My uncle lives at Mumbai with his family. Correct the preposition.

My uncle lives in Mumbai with his family.
Why: Use "in" with cities and large places.
The kids were jumping on the puddles after the rain. Is "on" right?

The kids were jumping in the puddles after the rain.
Why: Use "in" for being inside water.
Where has gone your brother? Please correct my question.

Where has your brother gone?
Why: In a question the subject goes between the helper verb "has" and the main verb "gone".
How many students there are in your class? Can you fix the order?

How many students are there in your class?
Why: In a question the verb "are" comes before "there".
He doesn't live here, doesn't he? Check the end of my sentence.

He doesn't live here, does he?
Why: A negative statement takes a positive tag, so use "does he".
Is this phrase okay? Please give me two papers for the drawing class.

Please give me two sheets of paper for the drawing class.
Why: "Paper" as a material is uncountable, so count it with "sheets of".
Her hairs are very long and black. Is the plural right?

Her hair is very long and black.
Why: "Hair" is uncountable here, so it takes no -s and a singular verb.
The babys were sleeping while the ladys prepared dinner. Please check the spelling.

The babies were sleeping while the ladies prepared dinner.
Why: A noun ending in a consonant plus -y changes to -ies in the plural.
The rice are ready, so please bring the plates. What is wrong?

The rice is ready, so please bring the plates.
Why: "Rice" is uncountable, so it takes a singular verb.
The weathers in Shimla is cold in winter. Please fix it.

The weather in Shimla is cold in winter.
Why: "Weather" is uncountable, so it has no plural form and takes the singular verb "is".
Of the three brothers, Ravi is the taller. Is that correct?

Of the three brothers, Ravi is the tallest.
Why: Use the superlative "tallest" when you compare three or more people.
Today's class was much interesting than yesterday's. Fix this, please.

Today's class was much more interesting than yesterday's.
Why: A long adjective like "interesting" forms its comparative with "more" before "than".
My grades are better than Sam. Is the comparison right?

My grades are better than Sam's.
Why: You must compare like with like, so "grades" are compared with "Sam's" grades.
Whom is calling at this hour? Check the first word.

Who is calling at this hour?
Why: "Who" is the subject of "is calling". "Whom" is used for the object.
I like them mangoes from the corner shop. Please correct.

I like those mangoes from the corner shop.
Why: "Them" is an object pronoun. Before a noun, use the demonstrative "those".
Please help you to some tea and snacks, everyone. What is wrong?

Please help yourself to some tea and snacks, everyone.
Why: The fixed phrase is "help yourself", with a reflexive pronoun.
Is this book your's? Check my pronoun.

Is this book yours?
Why: The possessive pronoun "yours" never takes an apostrophe. "Your's" is not a word.
I will visit my uncle next weak. Please check the spelling.

I will visit my uncle next week.
Why: "Week" is seven days. "Weak" means not strong.
Come hear and sit beside me. Which word is wrong?

Come here and sit beside me.
Why: "Here" means this place. "Hear" is what you do with your ears.
Let's take a brake from studying and have some tea. Check the spelling.

Let's take a break from studying and have some tea.
Why: A "break" is a short rest. A "brake" stops a vehicle.
My socks have a whole in them. Is that the right word?

My socks have a hole in them.
Why: A "hole" is an opening. "Whole" means complete.
Mr Khan our neighbour is a retired pilot. Please fix the punctuation.

Mr Khan, our neighbour, is a retired pilot.
Why: Commas go around extra information about the person.
I bought two kilos of apple's from the market. What is wrong?

I bought two kilos of apples from the market.
Why: A plural noun does not take an apostrophe. The apostrophe is for possession or contractions.
we are meeting on monday in mumbai. Is the capitalisation right?

We are meeting on Monday in Mumbai.
Why: Start a sentence with a capital letter, and capitalise days and place names.
Sam asked, "Can I borrow your pen"? Where does the question mark go?

Sam asked, "Can I borrow your pen?"
Why: The quoted words are a question, so the question mark goes inside the closing quotation mark.
I want to do an appointment with the dentist. Is "do" right?

I want to make an appointment with the dentist.
Why: "Make an appointment" is the fixed phrase.
Let me do a photo of you and your sister. Please correct it.

Let me take a photo of you and your sister.
Why: "Take a photo" is the usual phrase for using a camera.
My friend won me at chess yesterday. What is the correct verb?

My friend beat me at chess yesterday.
Why: You "win" a game or prize, but you "beat" a person.
Every night I see TV for an hour. Is "see" right?

Every night I watch TV for an hour.
Why: "Watch" is used for television and things that move or happen. "See" means to notice with your eyes.
My parents want me becoming a doctor. Please fix this.

My parents want me to become a doctor.
Why: "Want" with an object is followed by "to" and the base verb.
Can you help me to carrying this box upstairs? What is wrong?

Can you help me carry this box upstairs?
Why: After "help" use the base verb ("carry") or "to carry", never "to" with -ing.
She refused helping me with the tickets. Please correct.

She refused to help me with the tickets.
Why: The verb "refuse" is followed by "to" and the base verb.
He keeps to ask the same question every day. Which part is wrong?

He keeps asking the same question every day.
Why: "Keep" meaning "continue" is followed by an -ing form.
Is the tense right? My sister has been learning the violin for two years.

The tense is fine.
Why: The present perfect continuous with "for two years" shows an action that began in the past and still continues.
Please proofread: She is famous for her sweets, and people travel from other cities to buy them.

Nothing to fix here.
Why: "Famous for" is the right pair, and "to buy" shows purpose after "travel".
Should I use "since" or "for"? I haven't seen him since Tuesday.

"Since" is correct here.
Why: "Since" is used with a starting point such as "Tuesday", and the present perfect "haven't seen" matches it.
Do both verbs match? The children were playing quietly while their parents were talking.

Yes, both verbs match.
Why: Both clauses use the past continuous for two actions that were happening at the same time.
Has or have? Neither of us has finished the project yet.

"Has" is correct.
Why: "Neither" is singular, so it takes "has". With "of us", the verb still agrees with "neither".
Dhruv said that he will join us later. Is "will" right in reported speech?

Dhruv said that he would join us later.
Why: After a past reporting verb like "said", "will" changes to "would".
I am reading this novel when you called me. Please fix the verb.

I was reading this novel when you called me.
Why: Use the past continuous for the longer action that was interrupted by "called".
My parents are married for twenty years. Can you fix the tense?

My parents have been married for twenty years.
Why: A state that began in the past and still continues needs the present perfect with "for".
Both of my sisters is musicians and plays in a band. Please check.

Both of my sisters are musicians and play in a band.
Why: "Both" is plural, so the verbs are "are" and "play".
The reason for the delay were the floods. What is wrong with the verb?

The reason for the delay was the floods.
Why: The subject is "reason", which is singular, so the verb is "was".
My uncle, who owns three shops, work late every day. Which verb needs changing?

My uncle, who owns three shops, works late every day.
Why: The subject of "work" is "uncle", which is singular, so the verb takes -s.
My brother wants to be an engineer, but my sister wants to be a artist. Check the articles.

My brother wants to be an engineer, but my sister wants to be an artist.
Why: Use "an" before a vowel sound, and "artist" begins with one.
We had a lunch at the canteen after the class. Is "a" needed?

We had lunch at the canteen after the class.
Why: Names of meals usually take no article.
Could you open window, please? It is very warm in here.

Could you open the window, please? It is very warm in here.
Why: A singular countable noun needs an article, and "the" fits because both people know which window.
The cake was divided in four equal parts. Is the preposition right?

The cake was divided into four equal parts.
Why: The verb "divide" is followed by "into" when it shows the parts that result.
Naveen insisted in paying the bill. Please correct this.

Naveen insisted on paying the bill.
Why: The verb "insist" takes the preposition "on", and the word after it takes -ing.
I will wait in the bus stop until you come. Which word is wrong?

I will wait at the bus stop until you come.
Why: Use "at" for a point or a specific stopping place.
Mira is very similar with her father. What should I change?

Mira is very similar to her father.
Why: The adjective "similar" is followed by "to".
Where I can find a good tailor? Please correct the order.

Where can I find a good tailor?
Why: In a question the helper verb "can" comes before the subject "I".
Is she knows the answer? Fix my question.

Does she know the answer?
Why: "Is" cannot be combined with the main verb "know". Use "does" and the base form.
The tree dropped all its leafs on the path. Check the plural.

The tree dropped all its leaves on the path.
Why: Many nouns ending in -f change to -ves in the plural, so "leaf" becomes "leaves".
Her jewelleries are kept in the locker. Is the noun right?

Her jewellery is kept in the locker.
Why: "Jewellery" is uncountable, so it has no plural and takes "is".
There are two mistake in this paragraph. Please fix.

There are two mistakes in this paragraph.
Why: A plural noun after "two" needs -s.
This lake is deeper than any other lakes in the state. What is wrong?

This lake is deeper than any other lake in the state.
Why: After "any other" the noun is singular.
Rani is as smart than her sister. Please correct.

Rani is as smart as her sister.
Why: A comparison of equals uses "as ... as". "Than" belongs with a comparative.
This phone is expensive than that one. What is missing?

This phone is more expensive than that one.
Why: A comparison with "than" needs a comparative form, so "more" is added before "expensive".
Yourself and your brother are invited to the prize ceremony. Is this right?

You and your brother are invited to the prize ceremony.
Why: A reflexive pronoun like "yourself" cannot be the subject. Use "you".
This is the book what I told you about. Please fix it.

This is the book that I told you about.
Why: "What" cannot join a noun to a describing clause. Use "that" or "which".
Her and Meena are cousins from Nagpur. What is wrong?

She and Meena are cousins from Nagpur.
Why: The subject of the sentence needs the subject pronoun "she", not "her".
Tom invited we to his birthday party. Which word is wrong?

Tom invited us to his birthday party.
Why: "Us" is the object pronoun after the verb "invited".
I was board during the long speech. Check the spelling.

I was bored during the long speech.
Why: "Bored" describes feeling uninterested. A "board" is a flat piece of wood.
I did not no the answer to the last question. Which word is wrong?

I did not know the answer to the last question.
Why: "Know" means to have knowledge. "No" is the opposite of yes.
Our grandmother told us a tail about a clever crow. Please check this.

Our grandmother told us a tale about a clever crow.
Why: A "tale" is a story. A "tail" is part of an animal.
We sat by the see and watched the boats. Is the spelling right?

We sat by the sea and watched the boats.
Why: "Sea" is the salty water, and "see" is what your eyes do.
The plain landed at Chennai just before noon. What is wrong?

The plane landed at Chennai just before noon.
Why: A "plane" is an aircraft. "Plain" means simple or flat.
The teacher said that, we should read daily. Is the comma needed?

The teacher said that we should read daily.
Why: Do not put a comma between a reporting verb and the "that" clause.
The meeting is at five o'clock. Will you be there. Fix the punctuation.

The meeting is at five o'clock. Will you be there?
Why: A direct question ends with a question mark.
I dont know where Ive kept my glasses. What is missing?

I don't know where I've kept my glasses.
Why: A contraction takes an apostrophe where letters are left out.
Zoya took a prize in the quiz last week. Is "took" the right verb?

Zoya won a prize in the quiz last week.
Why: "Win a prize" is the usual phrase for getting a prize in a contest.
We are going to pass the holidays at my grandmother's village. What is wrong?

We are going to spend the holidays at my grandmother's village.
Why: "Spend the holidays" is the usual phrase for time away. "Pass" sounds dated here.
Arjun is doing good progress in maths. Please correct.

Arjun is making good progress in maths.
Why: "Make progress" is the fixed phrase. You do not "do" progress.
I made my homework before dinner. Is "made" correct?

I did my homework before dinner.
Why: "Do homework" is the fixed phrase. "Make" is used for things you create, not for schoolwork.
We discussed to buy a second-hand car. Fix the verb form.

We discussed buying a second-hand car.
Why: The verb "discuss" is followed by an -ing form, not "to".
My teacher advised me to took notes in class. What is wrong?

My teacher advised me to take notes in class.
Why: After "to" use the base verb, not a past form.
Her mother let her to go to the fair alone. Please correct.

Her mother let her go to the fair alone.
Why: "Let" is followed by the base verb without "to".
Rekha asked me help her carry the boxes. Fix this, please.

Rekha asked me to help her carry the boxes.
Why: "Ask" with an object is followed by "to" and the base verb.
We're planning to going to Ooty in May. Which part is wrong?

We're planning to go to Ooty in May.
Why: After "planning to", use the base verb.
I am hearing a strange noise from the kitchen. Is the tense right?

I hear a strange noise from the kitchen.
Why: Verbs of sense such as "hear" are normally not used in the continuous form.
Is "such a big" correct? I have never seen such a big rainbow.

Yes, "such a big" is correct.
Why: "Such" goes before "a + adjective + noun", and the present perfect "have never seen" is right for life experience.
Is anything wrong here? The roads were closed because of the heavy snow.

Nothing is wrong.
Why: "Because of" is followed by a noun phrase, and "heavy" is the usual word for snow.
Please check: My brother and his friends are going to the match on Sunday.

This sentence is fine as it is.
Why: The subject "my brother and his friends" is plural, so "are" is right, and "on Sunday" is the correct preposition for a day.
He gave me some useful information about the course. Does this need changing?

It needs no change.
Why: "Information" is uncountable, so "some" is right and no -s is needed.
Is "since" right here? She has lived in Hyderabad since she was six.

It is right as written.
Why: "Since" points to the moment she was six, and the present perfect "has lived" fits an action that continues now.
I am going to the temple every Tuesday with my grandfather. What is wrong with the tense?

I go to the temple every Tuesday with my grandfather.
Why: A regular habit uses the simple present, not the present continuous.
It's the third time she has forgot her umbrella this week. Check the verb.

It's the third time she has forgotten her umbrella this week.
Why: The present perfect needs the past participle "forgotten", not "forgot".
We watched the sunrise, and then we are eating breakfast at the cafe. Please fix this.

We watched the sunrise, and then we ate breakfast at the cafe.
Why: Both actions happened in the past, so the second verb must be in the past too.
If you heat ice, it melted. Is the second verb right?

If you heat ice, it melts.
Why: A general fact uses the present simple in both parts of the sentence.
Mangoes is my favourite fruit in summer. Which verb is right?

Mangoes are my favourite fruit in summer.
Why: "Mangoes" is plural, so the verb is "are".
Every girl and boy have a notebook and a pencil. Please check the verb.

Every girl and boy has a notebook and a pencil.
Why: "Every" is followed by a singular verb, even with two nouns joined by "and".
Priya and her mother goes to the market on Saturdays. Fix it, please.

Priya and her mother go to the market on Saturdays.
Why: Two people joined by "and" are plural, so the verb has no -s.
I have to go to bank today to deposit this cheque. Is an article missing?

I have to go to the bank today to deposit this cheque.
Why: A particular, known bank needs "the" before it.
We stayed at hotel near the lake last winter. What is missing?

We stayed at a hotel near the lake last winter.
Why: A singular countable noun that is mentioned for the first time takes "a".
She is wearing a red dress and the blue scarf. Is that correct?

She is wearing a red dress and a blue scarf.
Why: The scarf is new information, not one already known, so "a" is needed, not "the".
Mohan is doctor and his wife is a teacher. Please correct it.

Mohan is a doctor and his wife is a teacher.
Why: A job title after "is" needs "a" or "an".
I agree to you about the new timetable. Which word is wrong?

I agree with you about the new timetable.
Why: You agree "with" a person and "to" a plan.
She complained to me for the loud music. Is the preposition right?

She complained to me about the loud music.
Why: You complain "about" something, and "to" the person you tell.
We were surprised with the good news about the match. Please correct.

We were surprised at the good news about the match.
Why: "Surprised" is usually followed by "at" or "by".
I have a great respect to my teachers. What should I change?

I have great respect for my teachers.
Why: The noun "respect" takes "for", and "great respect" is uncountable, so it takes no "a".
What he told you yesterday after class? Please fix my question.

What did he tell you yesterday after class?
Why: A question needs the helper "did" before the subject, and the main verb then returns to the base form.
How much does cost this bag? Correct the word order, please.

How much does this bag cost?
Why: In a question the subject "this bag" comes after the helper verb "does" and before the main verb.
The wifes of both players cheered loudly from the stands. Check the plural.

The wives of both players cheered loudly from the stands.
Why: Nouns ending in -fe change to -ves in the plural.
There is a lot of traffics near the school at nine. Is the noun right?

There is a lot of traffic near the school at nine.
Why: "Traffic" is uncountable, so it has no plural.
Our cat caught three mouses in the store room. Is this the right plural?

Our cat caught three mice in the store room.
Why: "Mouse" has an irregular plural, "mice".
This soup is very hotter than yesterday's. Please correct.

This soup is much hotter than yesterday's.
Why: "Very" cannot go with a comparative. Use "much" before words like "hotter".
He is not so tall like his brother. Please correct my comparison.

He is not as tall as his brother.
Why: Use "as ... as" for comparisons of equal degree, in negatives too.
Meena is cleverer from me, but I am faster. What is wrong?

Meena is cleverer than me, but I am faster.
Why: A comparative is followed by "than", not "from".
All of we students were sorry to see the teacher leave. Is this right?

All of us students were sorry to see the teacher leave.
Why: After "of" use the object pronoun "us", not the subject pronoun "we".
It was hard for I to say goodbye at the station. Which pronoun is wrong?

It was hard for me to say goodbye at the station.
Why: After a preposition such as "for", use the object pronoun "me".
The two friends hugged themselves when they met after the holidays. Please check.

The two friends hugged each other when they met after the holidays.
Why: A reflexive pronoun means the same person acts and receives. For two people doing the same to one another, use "each other".
Please mark the date on the calender. Check my spelling.

Please mark the date on the calendar.
Why: "Calendar" ends in -ar, not -er. A helpful way to remember it is that it has "end" in the middle.
At the begining of the year we chose our class monitor. Is the spelling right?

At the beginning of the year we chose our class monitor.
Why: "Beginning" has a double n because the stress falls on the last part when -ing is added.
Our bus fair has gone up again this month. Is that the right word?

Our bus fare has gone up again this month.
Why: "Fare" is the price of a journey. A "fair" is an event with stalls and rides.
I bought a kilo of flower to make chapatis. Which word is wrong?

I bought a kilo of flour to make chapatis.
Why: "Flour" is ground grain for baking. A "flower" is the part of a plant that blooms.
I wrote my plan in my dairy last night. What is wrong with the word?

I wrote my plan in my diary last night.
Why: A "diary" is a book for daily notes. A "dairy" is where milk products are made.
It is neccessary to carry an ID card in the office. Please check the spelling.

It is necessary to carry an ID card in the office.
Why: "Necessary" is spelled with one c and a double s.
Hurry up we are late for the show. Fix the punctuation.

Hurry up. We are late for the show.
Why: Two complete sentences need a full stop between them.
Yes I will come to your party and bring sweets. What is missing?

Yes, I will come to your party and bring sweets.
Why: A comma follows an opening "yes" or "no".
Rajesh is my friends brother and he plays hockey. Please fix the punctuation.

Rajesh is my friend's brother and he plays hockey.
Why: The brother belongs to one friend, so add an apostrophe and -s to the singular noun.
Let's make a party for Diwali on the terrace. Is "make" right?

Let's have a party for Diwali on the terrace.
Why: The usual phrase is "have a party". "Throw a party" is also common.
My uncle said a joke at dinner and everyone laughed. Is "said" right?

My uncle told a joke at dinner and everyone laughed.
Why: The fixed phrase is "tell a joke".
It is a big pleasure to meet you, Ms Thomas. Please correct.

It is a great pleasure to meet you, Ms Thomas.
Why: "Great pleasure" is the fixed phrase. "Big" is not used with "pleasure".
Please do a cup of tea for me while I finish this. Is "do" correct?

Please make a cup of tea for me while I finish this.
Why: You "make" a drink or a meal. "Do" is not used for it.
I have difficulty to sleep when it is very hot. Please correct this.

I have difficulty sleeping when it is very hot.
Why: "Have difficulty" is followed by an -ing form.
The student admitted to have broken the window. Fix the verb form.

The student admitted breaking the window.
Why: The verb "admit" is followed by an -ing form.
They have decided buying a small shop in the market. What is wrong?

They have decided to buy a small shop in the market.
Why: "Decide" is followed by "to" and the base verb.
I forgot telling him about the meeting, so he missed it. Is the verb pattern right?

I forgot to tell him about the meeting, so he missed it.
Why: "Forget to" is used for something you did not do. "Forget -ing" is for something you did and cannot remember.
She has been to Kerala twice. Is "been to" right here?

That is the right phrase.
Why: "Been to" is the normal way to talk about visits that are finished, and "twice" fits the present perfect.
There isn't any milk left, so I'll buy some. Should it be "any" or "some"?

Both are used correctly.
Why: "Any" goes in negative statements and "some" goes in positive ones.
My brother is taller than I am. Is "I am" correct, or should it be "me"?

Your sentence is correct as written.
Why: With "than I am" the full clause is used, so the subject pronoun "I" is right. "Than me" is also common in speech.
The children's drawings are on the wall. Please check the apostrophe.

Nothing needs changing.
Why: "Children" is already plural, so the possessive adds apostrophe and -s.
He doesn't know how to swim yet. Is "doesn't" right with "he"?

Yes, that's correct.
Why: "He" is third person singular, so "doesn't" is right, and "know" stays in the base form.
She don't eat spicy food, so we ordered less chilli. Please fix any mistakes.

She doesn't eat spicy food, so we ordered less chilli.
Why: With "she" (third person singular) the negative helper is "doesn't", not "don't".
We reached to the station ten minutes before the train left. Is "reached to" okay?

We reached the station ten minutes before the train left.
Why: "Reach" takes its object directly, with no "to". You could also say "arrived at the station".
My manager gave me a feedback on the report yesterday. Anything to change?

My manager gave me feedback on the report yesterday.
Why: "Feedback" is uncountable, so it does not take "a".
Me and Kavya went to the mela on Sunday. Can you polish this?

Kavya and I went to the mela on Sunday.
Why: As the subject, use "I", not "me". It is also polite to name the other person first.
Our team has won the match yesterday. What should I change?

Our team won the match yesterday.
Why: A finished time such as "yesterday" goes with the simple past, not the present perfect.
I have a toothache and I am scared to go the dentist. Is a word missing?

I have a toothache and I am scared to go to the dentist.
Why: Yes, "to" is missing. We say "go to" before a place or a person we visit.
The sunset over the lake was absolutly beautiful. Is "absolutly" spelled correctly?

The sunset over the lake was absolutely beautiful.
Why: "Absolute" keeps its final "e" when -ly is added, so the adverb is "absolutely".
The bill came to five hundred rupees, and I payed it by cash. Please fix.

The bill came to five hundred rupees, and I paid it in cash.
Why: The past tense of "pay" is "paid". The usual phrase is "pay in cash".
Their are two fans in my bedroom, but one doesn't works. Help me with this.

There are two fans in my bedroom, but one doesn't work.
Why: "There are" states that something exists, while "their" shows ownership. After "doesn't", the verb stays in the base form.
The book which I borrowed it from the library is very interesting. Is something extra?

The book which I borrowed from the library is very interesting.
